decisive_spans.text: an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of his forehead
histopathologic examination: Image C: Scanning view shows predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
Image D: High-power view shows inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis

response.rationale: Morphea is strongly supported by the characteristic 'arc-shaped, depressed skin groove' and the histopathological findings of lymphocytic infiltrates and hyaline fat necrosis. While Frontal fibrosing alopecia also presents with a depressed groove and hair loss, the specific histopathological findings are more indicative of Morphea. Alopecia areata is less likely given the negative hair pull test and the specific groove. Lichen planopilaris is contradicted by the fat necrosis.
